div.head: Iudex 12
div.ab: Impii iudices, iuxta uerba sapientium, sicut rapaces lupi nespere nil residuant usque mane, id est de presenti solum uita cogitant; de futura nichil considerant.
Þa únrihtwisan deman, æfter witegan cwyde, swa swa wulfas on æfne, ne læfað náwiht oð morgen: þæt ys, þæt hi be þisses anweardan lifes ongehyðnesse ðenceað ⁊ nawiht be þæs towerdan.
Unjust judges follow the prophet’s saying: like wolves in the evening, they leave nothing for morning. That is, they think about this present life’s advantages and nothing about the next.

Die ungerechten Richter lassen nach des Propheten Spruch, so wie Wölfe am Abend nichts bis zum Morgen übrig: d. h. dass sie an das Vortheilhafte dieses gegenwärtigen Lebens denken und nicht an das des zukünftigen.
Unjust judges, according to the prophet's saying, like wolves in the evening, leave nothing until morning: that is, they think of the advantage of this present life and not of the life to come.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
